title: Redwood All-Hands - January 2026
summary: Leadership provided a high-level review of Q4/2025 performance, product priorities for H1 2026 (Dedicated capacity improvements, Private deployment enhancements, and Redwood Optimize expansion), hiring plans, and compliance milestones. Open Q&A covered latency SLAs, Dedicated pricing, and next steps for region expansion and pilot signups.
action_items: Tom Barlow: share performance benchmark deck and internal latency spreadsheet with leadership and product by 2026-01-29
Maya Singh: publish updated roadmap doc (Dedicated autoscale, Optimize batching recommendations) by 2026-02-02
Aisha Patel: prepare enterprise pricing playbook and renewal talking points for key accounts by 2026-02-05
Security Team: finalize SOC 2 Type II evidence bundle and share with Sales by 2026-02-10
next_steps: Leadership to review FY26 targets in the leadership offsite (calendar invite to follow)
Enable pilot signups for Private deployment in EU region in limited capacity next quarter
Schedule focused technical deep dive on KV cache and autoscaling with select customers (SE-led)
transcript:
[00:00] Emily: Okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. We'll get started in a minute, just waiting for a couple more people to trickle in, uh, sorry about the slight delay.
[00:16] Emily: Welcome to the January all-hands, quick agenda - company results, product updates, hiring/org, security, then Q&A.
[00:30] Carlos: Quick note, we did flip the new kernel selector into canary on Monday; early numbers look promising on 95th percentile latency. There are some outliers around long-contexts we need to iron out.
[00:47] Tom: Yeah just to add, the KV cache changes improved throughput for chat-heavy workloads, but we saw a regression on small batch latencies that we think is due to the batching policy.
[01:05] Maya: We'll put up the roadmap slide; main priorities for H1 are Dedicated autoscale with burst, Private EU region GA, and Redwood Optimize - particularly the batching and quantization recommendation engine.
[01:24] Emily: Thanks. On business - Q4 numbers: ARR expansion was up 28% quarter-over-quarter, churn held steady at 3.1%, and we hit a small but important milestone: 15 enterprise contracts for Dedicated. These are early but meaningful.
[01:46] Aisha: Pipeline looks healthy, lots of inbound from platform teams wanting Private for data residency. The ask we keep hearing is predictable latency and clear cost profile.
[02:03] Speaker 6 (Finance): Margins improved as we rolled out some of the quantized variants; per-token cost dropped ~8% in aggregate, still more to do on GPU utilization.
[02:22] Emily: Great. Security update?
[02:28] Speaker 7 (Security): SOC 2 Type II is on track - audit firm gave provisional sign-off for evidence collection; aiming for Type II complete by mid-February. Also we've finalized KMS recommendations for Private deployments.
[02:44] Carlos: On Private, engineering is focused on the installer and the private control plane - customers asked for better offline upgrade story and tight integration with customer KMS/HSM. That work is in sprint 4.
[03:02] Tom: For Dedicated, we're focusing on autoscale policies and predictable tail latency. The plan is to let customers pin a latency SLO and we'll route to capacity tiers accordingly; fallback to hosted variants if capacity constrained.
[03:20] Maya: On product ops, we're launching a new rollout experience - canaries, A/B, and automatic fallbacks by model family. This should help enterprise customers mitigate regressions.
[03:36] Emily: Hiring - hiring freeze lifted for critical IC roles. We'll prioritize SRE, runtime engineers, and sales engineers for enterprise support. Expect 25 open roles by end of February.
[03:50] Aisha: We also need more Solutions Engineers to support Dedicated pilots; onboarding ramp for SEs will be ~3 weeks with certs.
[04:05] Emily: Open Q&A now.
[04:10] Speaker 8 (Eng): Quick question on SLA wording - can we commit to 99.9% uptime for Dedicated or do we need caveats?
[04:18] Carlos: We can commit to an uptime SLA in contracts but latency SLOs will be dependent on configured capacity and model. We'll provide latency bands and pricing tiers.
[04:31] Speaker 9 (Sales): Pricing question - Dedicated pricing for committed capacity vs burst - how are we structuring overage charges?
[04:38] Aisha: The playbook is coming, but high level: reserved monthly commit + burst credits at a predictable per-token uplift. We want predictable economics - that's our sales pitch.
[04:53] Speaker 10 (Customer Success): Any changes to audit logs and retention for Private? Some customers want 7+ year retention for specific logs.
[05:02] Speaker 7 (Security): We'll add configurable retention options, but long-tail retention may be an add-on given storage costs. We'll document retention SLAs.
[05:18] Emily: Quick product demo - Maya?
[05:22] Maya: Sure, just a 90-second walkthrough of the new Optimize tab - shows per-route token economics, recommended quant profiles, and batch configuration suggestions. (short pause) You'll notice the suggested profile is model and workload specific; it's been tuned with internal evals.
[05:45] Tom: On the infra side, early batch tuning saved one of our customer pilots ~20% on GPU cost without noticeable quality regression. That's the kind of win we want to scale.
[06:02] Carlos: Technical note - the kernel selector change is still experimental; disabled by default for some model families. We need more regression tests around long sequences.
[06:16] Speaker 11 (Legal): Procurement update - our standard enterprise contract templates will include data processing annex and specific clauses for Private deployments. Legal is preparing playbooks for renewal deals.
[06:32] Emily: Alright, Q&A from Slack - first question: region expansion timeline for APAC?
[06:39] Maya: We're targeting a small APAC cluster pilot late Q2, but GA depends on demand and partner readiness.
[06:47] Speaker 12 (Eng): Will we support on-prem air-gapped installs for regulated customers?
[06:52] Carlos: Yes, planned as an advanced Private offering with additional security review and professional services.
[07:00] Speaker 13 (Sales): Do we have benchmark artifacts to share with customers when they ask about latency vs cost tradeoffs?
[07:06] Tom: Yes, we'll produce a benchmarking pack (per-model latency/cost spreadsheet) - I'll share it with Sales and SEs this week.
[07:16] Emily: Great. Anything else? (short pause) Okay, final notes: leadership offsite coming next month, calendar invite to follow. We'll post the recording and slides. Thank you all.
[07:33] Emily: Recap - benchmarks to Sales, roadmap doc from Maya, SOC2 evidence to Sales, onboard new SEs, publish hiring plan.
[07:45] Speaker 14 (Someone in background): Thanks, great work team.
[07:50] Emily: Meeting adjourned.

-- End of transcript --
